## Problem 1

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(1)

birthday_match = function(n) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)
  any(duplicated(birthdays))
}

birthday_results =
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |>
  mutate(
    shared_birthday = map_lgl(group_size, birthday_match)
  ) |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarize(
    probability = mean(shared_birthday)
  )

birthday_results |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Group Size",
    y = "Probability of Shared Birthday"
  )
```

The probability of sharing a birthday increases as the group size increases. With around 23 people, the probability is about 50%. By 50 people, the probability is approximately 97%.

## Problem 2

```{r}
full_df =
  tibble(
    files = list.files("data/"),
    path = str_c("data/", files)
  ) |>
mutate(data = map(path, \(x) read_csv(x, show_col_types = FALSE)))|>
  unnest(cols = data)
```


```{r}
tidy_df =
  full_df |>
  mutate(
    files = str_replace(files, ".csv", ""),
    arm = str_sub(files, 1, 3)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    week_1:week_8,
    names_to = "week",
    values_to = "outcome",
    names_prefix = "week_"
  ) |>
  mutate(week = as.numeric(week)) |>
  select(arm, subject_id = files, week, outcome)

tidy_df
```


```{r}
tidy_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = outcome, group = subject_id, color = arm)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_path() +
  facet_grid(~arm) +
  labs(
    x = "Week",
    y = "Outcome"
  )
```

The control group stays relatively stable over time, while the experimental group shows an increasing trend. There is some variation between subjects in both groups.
